trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: The Platinum pops the moment the other 54 trophies are yours. There is no extra task — it is a receipt for the whole run, so plan the run, not this trophy.

steps.text: Earn the other 54 trophies in any order; the Platinum unlocks automatically with the last one.
Track the count in this guide — the header meter shows your running total out of 55.
No online play, DLC or second playthrough is needed; one run on one save is enough.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: The opening mission. Jason's first job on the water teaches the basics and ends the moment the catch is in — pure story, nothing to prepare.

steps.text: Start a new game and play the opening mission Gone Fishing as Jason.
Follow the on-screen prompts through the fishing beats; no fail state blocks the trophy.
Finish the mission and the trophy pops at the results screen.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Finish every main mission in Chapter 1. The chapter closes on its own once the last mission ends, so just keep playing the story.

steps.text: Play through all Chapter 1 main missions in order.
Do the balcony meditation with Lucia after Down to Earth before the chapter ends (see Positive Mental Attitude).
Complete the chapter's final mission and the trophy unlocks as Chapter 2 begins.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Chapter 2 closes the same way Chapter 1 did: finish its main missions and the trophy follows. Use this chapter to start scanning vehicles and studying animals.

steps.text: Play through all Chapter 2 main missions in order.
Scan new vehicles with the WAiNK app and study new animals through binoculars along the way — both count toward the 100% checklist later.
Complete the chapter's final mission; the trophy pops as Chapter 3 begins.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: The Vice City chapter. Keep the story moving and the trophy arrives at the chapter break; Stranger chains that opened in Chapters 1–2 are worth a detour here.

steps.text: Play through all Chapter 3 main missions in order.
Check the map for Stranger icons between missions — Andy, Kenton and the others open their chains in this stretch.
Keep a manual save at the start of the chapter, in case you want a backup before the later missions.
Complete the chapter's final mission; the trophy pops as Chapter 4 begins.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Chapter 4 is the longest stretch of the story and the one that opens the big bank vaults. Finish it and the trophy is yours; do the optional vault mission before the chapter ends.

steps.text: Play through all Chapter 4 main missions in order.
Take the optional mission That's Where The Money Is… when it appears — it unlocks the large bank vaults used by Maximum Withdrawal.
Keep a manual save at the start of the chapter; there is no mission replay to fall back on.
Complete the chapter's final mission; the trophy pops as Chapter 5 begins.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: The last story mission. One of only two Gold trophies, it marks the end of the campaign — after it, the whole map stays open in free roam for cleanup.

steps.text: Finish Chapters 1–4, then play through Chapter 5's main missions.
Make a manual save right before the final mission — it is the last story beat and there is no replay.
Complete the final mission and the trophy pops at the credits.
After the credits the 100% checklist appears under Progress > Stats > 100% Completion.

dispute.versionA: Exophase and PSNProfiles word the requirement as 'Complete the final mission.'
dispute.versionB: Beebom and CULTR describe the same trophy as finishing Chapter 5.
dispute.call: Same unlock either way — the final mission is the end of Chapter 5, so both wordings point at one moment.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: A story mission early in the run. Play it as the story presents it — no side requirement, no preparation, just the mission itself.

steps.text: Reach the Breakfast Run mission in the story and start it from the mission marker.
Follow the mission objectives to the end; driving and on-foot beats both count toward the finish.
Complete the mission and the trophy pops at the results screen.
If the mission fails, retry it from the checkpoint — progress inside the mission is kept.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: The first big heist of the story. It plays as a set-piece mission — follow the plan, survive the escape, and the trophy lands with the payout.

steps.text: Reach The Cartel Heist in the story and start it from the mission marker.
Play through the setup and the heist itself; the mission guides each phase.
Survive the escape sequence to the end of the mission.
Complete the mission and the trophy pops at the results screen.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: A story mission in the early chapters. Nothing to set up in advance — the mission marker appears as the story reaches it.

steps.text: Reach the Child's Play mission in the story and start it from the mission marker.
Follow the mission objectives through to the end.
Complete the mission and the trophy pops at the results screen.
If the mission fails, retry it from the checkpoint — progress inside the mission is kept.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: A story mission in the middle chapters. It unlocks through the story alone, so the only job is to keep playing the campaign.

steps.text: Reach the Headliners mission in the story and start it from the mission marker.
Follow the mission objectives through to the end.
Complete the mission and the trophy pops at the results screen.
If the mission fails, retry it from the checkpoint — progress inside the mission is kept.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: A story mission built around the airport. The mission itself teaches the approach — take the takedown as the story stages it.

steps.text: Reach the VCIA Takedown mission in the story and start it from the mission marker.
Follow the mission objectives through the airport sequence.
Complete the mission and the trophy pops at the results screen.
If the mission fails, retry it from the checkpoint — progress inside the mission is kept.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: A late-story operation mission. It is story-only, so no grinding or side prep is needed — arrive, run the operation, finish it.

steps.text: Reach the Operation Savage Glory mission in the story and start it from the mission marker.
Follow the mission objectives through the operation.
Complete the mission and the trophy pops at the results screen.
If the mission fails, retry it from the checkpoint — progress inside the mission is kept.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: The hardest trophy in the set and the whole reason the platinum takes ~200 hours. The checklist only appears after the credits, but everything you did during the story already counts — and the thresholds are lenient, closer to 60% of true completion than 100%.

steps.text: Finish the story first: the checklist stays hidden until the credits, under Progress > Stats > 100% Completion.
Clear the robbery block first — 39 Gang Operations, 22 Bank Jobs, 7 Payday Loan Jobs, 34 of 35 Smash 'N' Grabs, 50 of 91 Stick Ups and 8 vaults.
Fence $100,000 in narcotics, $100,000 in jewelry, $250,000 in Marked Bills and $200,000 in vehicles.
Work the collectibles block: 5 of 7 Kenton sets, 15 of 18 card sets, 100 WAiNK scans, 33 underwater discoveries, 30 magazines, 15 of 18 meditations and 100 flamingos.
Finish the activities block: 30 unique races won, 10 race golds, 42 shooting range golds, 42 drone time trials, 300 stunts, 70 of 80 challenges and all 15 of Bret's Target Decks.
Close the discovery block: 200 of 277 base-model vehicles, 50 of 66 weapons and 100 of 255 animals — skip the rest, the checklist does not want them all.
Check the list after each block; the trophy pops the moment the last line ticks over.

dispute.topic: How long does the platinum really take?
dispute.versionA: PowerPyx and KeenGamer put the platinum at about 200 hours, with the checklist at roughly 60% of true completion.
dispute.versionB: PushSquare warns to expect up to 300 hours or more for the full run.
dispute.call: 200 hours fits the checklist thresholds as published; 300 hours is the safe budget if you chase everything instead of just the checklist lines.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Land 250 stunts anywhere in Leonida. The game counts 397 stunts in total and the 100% checklist wants 300, so this trophy comes first if you keep stunt-hunting while you travel.

steps.text: Stunts register as you play — jumps, near misses, airtime and the rest all feed the counter.
Any 250 of the 397 stunts count, so skip the awkward ones and repeat the easy kinds.
Flying under bridges is reported as the quickest repeatable stunt — loop a bridge run between other jobs.
Watch the counter in Progress > Stats; the trophy pops at 250 and the checklist still wants 300.
Pair stunt runs with WAiNK scans and vehicle spotting so the travel time does double duty.
Keep going to 300 stunts after this pops if you are chasing A Long Road.

dispute.versionA: PowerPyx and eGamers say any 250 of the 397 stunts count toward the trophy.
dispute.versionB: KeenGamer's table words it as 250 unique stunts, which reads stricter.
dispute.call: Treat it as any 250 — repeats of the easy kinds have been reported to count, and the 397 total gives huge slack either way.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Sample all nine activity types once. No winning needed — one round, one game, one visit each is enough to tick the box.

steps.text: Open the map and find the nine activity icons: arcade, pool, mini golf, basketball, bowling, darts, shooting range, races and fishing.
Play one round of each — a single arcade game, one pool match, one mini golf hole and so on.
The shooting range counts when you finish one challenge, win or lose.
The trophy pops after the ninth different activity; check the tracker below if you lose count.

dispute.versionA: KeenGamer lists nine activity types and the trophy description says 'each type of activity'.
dispute.versionB: No published list names the exact nine, and some guides count the arcade and the shooting range differently.
dispute.call: We count the nine map activities named in step 1 — if one does not tick, try the remaining venue type (bowling or darts) before assuming a bug.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Gold all 42 Shooting Range challenges. Every range counts the same way, so learn one range's rhythm and repeat it — the medals are not as hard as the number looks.

steps.text: Visit a shooting range and open its challenge list; each range holds several timed challenges.
Gold needs speed and accuracy together — steady aim beats spraying, and reloading early costs the medal.
Work range by range and use the counter below; the trophy pops at 42 of 42.
The same 42 golds are a line on the 100% checklist, so this trophy and A Long Road share the work.
If a challenge will not gold, switch weapon class for that range — some challenges suit a rifle, others a pistol.
Retrying a challenge is free and instant; grind the stubborn ones last when your aim is warm.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win one drone race at each of the 14 Top Fun locations. The races are short, and the same locations also host the 42 drone time trials the checklist wants.

steps.text: Find the 14 Top Fun drone race locations on the map — they spread across the whole state.
Win one race at each location; only the win counts, not the time.
PowerPyx counts 42 races across the 14 locations, so expect about three races per venue before you find the winning line.
The 42 drone time trials for the 100% checklist run at these same spots — do them on the same visit.
Use the counter below to track locations won; the trophy pops at 14 of 14.

dispute.topic: 14 locations, 42 races, 42 trials — which number is the trophy?
dispute.versionA: The trophy text says win a race at every location, and PowerPyx counts 14 locations with 42 races between them.
dispute.versionB: KeenGamer's checklist table lists 42 Drone Time Trials as the related requirement, which some readers mix up with the trophy.
dispute.call: The trophy is the 14 wins; the 42 time trials are a separate 100% checklist line at the same venues.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races. Road, off-road and street races all count — variety is the requirement, so do not grind one circuit twenty times.

steps.text: Open the map and pick race start points you have not won yet — each distinct race counts once.
Win 20 different races; repeats of a race you already won do not add to the count.
The checklist wants 30 unique races won, so keep going to 30 after this pops.
Race gold medals (10 of 13 for the checklist) are separate — a win without gold still counts here.
Use the counter below to track wins; the trophy pops at 20.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Out-fish Cal in one of his fishing challenges. Fishing is a calm minigame — the trick is steady reeling and not snapping the line when the fish runs.

steps.text: Meet Cal and take his fishing challenge from the mission marker or the dock where he waits.
Fish the challenge through: hook, reel steadily, ease off when the fish runs hard.
Beat Cal's catch and the trophy pops at the results screen.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Finish one arcade game, start to end. Any cabinet, any game — it is the easiest trophy in the set and it also ticks one of the nine activity types for Master of None.

steps.text: Walk into any arcade in Vice City or around Leonida and pick a cabinet.
Play the game through to its end screen — quitting early does not count.
The trophy pops when the game completes; it also counts as one activity type for Master of None.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Andy's whole chain, start to finish. Andy is Lucia-only, so switch to her when his missions appear, and start the chain early — quest givers go quiet for long stretches of the story.

steps.text: Find Andy's Stranger icon on the map and play his first mission as Lucia.
Keep returning to Andy's marker whenever a new mission in his chain appears.
Complete his final mission and the trophy pops at the results screen.
If Andy's icon vanishes for a while, keep playing the story — trophy quest givers return after the story in free roam.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Kenton's chain, including his treasure sets. Kenton goes quiet for stretches of the story, so start his missions the moment his icon shows and return whenever it reappears.

steps.text: Find Kenton's Stranger icon and play his first mission.
Work through his chain mission by mission; his treasure sets (5 of 7 for the checklist) run alongside.
Complete his final mission and the trophy pops at the results screen.
If Kenton's icon vanishes mid-story, keep playing — he returns later, and all trophy quest givers are back in free roam.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Billy's chain, start to finish. A bike-rider storyline that opens through a Stranger icon — start it early and keep answering his missions as they appear.

steps.text: Find Billy's Stranger icon on the map and play his first mission.
Keep returning to Billy's marker whenever a new mission in his chain appears.
Complete his final mission and the trophy pops at the results screen.
If Billy's icon vanishes for a while, keep playing the story — trophy quest givers return after the story in free roam.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Finish eight full Stranger mission strands. There are more than eight strangers in Leonida, so pick the eight whose chains you enjoy — but start them all early, because the chains have story windows.

steps.text: Open the map and take every Stranger icon you see: Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone, Bret and the rest.
A strand counts only when its whole chain is finished — one mission from a stranger is not a strand.
Finish eight complete strands; the five named finals (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone) are the natural core of the eight.
Bret's hunting chain and the other minor strangers fill the remaining slots if you are short.
The trophy pops at the eighth finished strand; use the counter below to track it.
Start every chain as soon as it unlocks — one guide reports story-linked windows on the Stranger chains, so do not leave them all to after the credits.

dispute.versionA: KeenGamer says eight qualifying Stranger mission strands, implying some strands do not count.
dispute.versionB: Exophase words it plainly as eight mission strands for strangers, with no qualifier.
dispute.call: Count the named-character chains (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone, Bret) plus any two full minor chains — the named six are the safe core.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Randy's chain, start to finish. Randy's deliveries also feed the 100 optional tasks on the checklist, so his missions do double duty toward A Long Road.

steps.text: Find Randy's Stranger icon on the map and play his first mission.
Keep returning to Randy's marker whenever a new mission in his chain appears.
Complete his final mission and the trophy pops at the results screen.
Randy's delivery runs count toward the 100 optional tasks, so do them as they come rather than batching them late.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Tyrone's chain, start to finish. Tyrone is Jason-only, so switch to him when his missions appear, and start the chain early — his labs also count toward the 100 optional tasks.

steps.text: Find Tyrone's Stranger icon on the map and play his first mission as Jason.
Keep returning to Tyrone's marker whenever a new mission in his chain appears.
Complete his final mission and the trophy pops at the results screen.
Tyrone's lab runs count toward the 100 optional tasks, so do them as they come rather than batching them late.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at all 18 spots across Leonida. The only trophy flagged as possibly missable: the first meditation, on the balcony at Jason's house, is offered only in Chapter 1. Do it the first morning it appears and the rest of the trophy is unmissable.

steps.text: After the mission Down to Earth, find Lucia at Jason's house in the morning; when she says she is going to meditate, follow her to the balcony and choose Accept.
Do the balcony meditation before Chapter 1 ends — it is the one session that never comes back.
After that, work the other spots in order: Smooth Sand (2–3), Swamp (4–5), Worn Stone (6–7), Red Rocks (8–9), Water Wheel (10–11), Jutting Cliff (12–13), Waterfall (14–15), Seaside (16–17).
Meditate at each spot as both Jason and Lucia where the game allows — a spot done with both counts twice toward the meditation total.
The final spot, Ascent on Mount Kalaga, is marked on the map only after the other spots are done.
Check the count in Progress > Collections > Exploration > Meditations; the trophy pops at 18.
Only 15 of 18 count toward the 100% checklist, so the last three are trophy-only — do not stop at 15.

dispute.topic: 18 meditations or 15 — and is the balcony one required?
dispute.versionA: PowerPyx says the balcony meditation raises the counter but is not marked as a Meditation Spot, so it is unclear whether it is required for the trophy.
dispute.versionB: KeenGamer and Beebom list 18 required spots with the balcony as spot 1, and the checklist wants only 15 of 18.
dispute.call: Do the balcony session in Chapter 1 no matter what — it costs two minutes and removes the only missable risk in the game.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt a unique animal for Bret. Bret's chain is the hunting strand: take his missions, track the animal he names, and bring it down. Which animal the trophy wants is the one detail the guides have not pinned down yet — see the dispute below.

steps.text: Find Bret's Stranger icon and play his hunting missions until he names the unique animal.
Track the animal with the hunting tools the mission provides; unique animals do not respawn on a timer like common ones.
Hunt the animal Bret names and complete the hunt to finish his chain.
Complete Bret's final mission and the trophy pops at the results screen.
If Bret's icon vanishes mid-story, keep playing — he returns later, and all trophy quest givers are back in free roam.

dispute.versionA: eGamers marks the animal as unconfirmed: the guides agree Bret wants a unique animal, but not which one.
dispute.versionB: KeenGamer's table lists the trophy as hunting a unique animal for Bret with no species named either.
dispute.call: Both sources agree the species is unconfirmed, so follow Bret's in-game mission text when it names the animal — that is the only authority that matters here.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Complete three full Collectible Card sets. There are 18 sets and 480 cards in the game, so pick the three smallest sets and hunt only those — the checklist wants 15 sets, but this trophy stops at three.

steps.text: Cards hide across Leonida in shops, houses and the open world; open the collection screen to see which sets are closest to complete.
Pick the three sets with the fewest missing cards and hunt only those first.
A set counts when every card in it is found; the trophy pops at the third completed set.
Use the counter below to track finished sets.
Keep going to 15 sets after this pops if you are chasing A Long Road — the same hunting routes serve both.
Cards found during the story already count, so check the collection screen before starting a dedicated hunt.

dispute.versionA: The trophy needs 3 complete sets.
dispute.versionB: The 100% checklist needs 15 of 18 sets, and some readers mix the two numbers up.
dispute.call: 3 for the trophy, 15 for the checklist — finish 3, celebrate, then keep hunting on the same routes.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: Scan 100 locations with the WAiNK app. The app is your scanner for the whole game — point it at landmarks, vehicles and oddities as you travel and the count climbs on its own.

steps.text: Open the WAiNK app on the in-game phone and point it at a location, vehicle or landmark until it registers.
Scan as you travel from the start of the game — 100 scans is a lot to batch at the end.
Landmarks, viewpoints and unusual spots all count; vehicles count too, and feed Whip It Good at the same time.
The checklist wants the same 100 scans, so this trophy and A Long Road share the work exactly.
Use the counter below to track scans; the trophy pops at 100.
If you are short late in the game, sweep Vice City's dense streets — scans are thickest where landmarks cluster.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Finish 50 of the game's 80 challenges. There are eight groups of ten, and you may skip the ten hardest — the checklist wants 70, but this trophy stops at 50, so take the easy fifty first.

steps.text: Open the challenges screen and pick the easiest group first — driving and combat challenges go fastest.
Complete 50 challenges in any mix; the trophy pops at 50 and the checklist still wants 70.
Skip the ten hardest challenges entirely — both guides agree they are not needed for the trophy.
Many challenges complete themselves while you chase other trophies, so check the count before grinding.
Use the counter below to track completed challenges.

dispute.versionA: The trophy needs 50 challenges completed.
dispute.versionB: The 100% checklist needs 70 of 80, and PowerPyx says to skip the hardest ten.
dispute.call: 50 for the trophy, 70 for the checklist — same screen, different finish lines.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: Get to four stars with your partner beside you, then lose the heat together. The wanted level is the hard part — escaping it is a driving job once the cops are off your tail.

steps.text: Bring your partner along, then raise your wanted level to four stars — robberies and shootouts raise it fastest.
Once you are at four stars, break line of sight and drive out of the red heat zone on the minimap.
Stay out of sight until the stars clear; the trophy pops when the heat is fully gone.
Bank vault robberies often bring the wanted level you need — pair this trophy with a vault run.
If the stars drop before you escape, raise them again and retry; nothing is lost on a failed attempt.

dispute.versionA: Both PowerPyx and GTABase point to a train tunnel north of Ambrosia as the escape spot.
dispute.versionB: The same guides say bank vault robberies often bring the wanted level on their own, with no tunnel needed.
dispute.call: Either route works — the tunnel is the reliable plan, the vault run is the convenient one. Use the tunnel if your first tries fail.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob three shops in a row with your partner while staying wanted the whole time. The chain is the trophy — if the wanted level clears between shops, the chain breaks and you start over.

steps.text: Bring your partner, then rob a first shop and get wanted — the chain starts with the first robbery.
Move straight to a second shop and rob it while still wanted; do not wait for the heat to die.
Hit a third shop the same way, still wanted, and the trophy should pop after the third.
North Vice City's jewelry stores sit close together, which keeps the travel time between robberies short.
If the trophy does not pop after the third, one guide says to rob a fourth shop before giving up.

dispute.versionA: The trophy text says three shops back-to-back, and most guides report it popping at the third.
dispute.versionB: GTABase says to rob a fourth shop if the trophy does not pop after the third.
dispute.call: Three is the requirement; the fourth is a workaround for a finicky trigger, not a fourth requirement.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 vehicles. Traffic is the hunting ground — scan or drive new models as you meet them and the counter fills up across the whole playthrough.

steps.text: Scan traffic with the WAiNK app as you travel; each new base model counts toward the 100.
Busy roads are the efficient spot — more traffic means more new models per minute.
The checklist wants 200 of 277 base models, so this trophy at 100 is the halfway mark, not the end.
Use the counter below to track discoveries; the trophy pops at 100.
Leave this for the cleanup stage if you are short — scanning traffic needs no mission and no unlock.

dispute.topic: Drive them or just scan them?
dispute.versionA: GTABase says scanning 100 different vehicles with WAiNK is enough, with no need to drive them.
dispute.versionB: The trophy text says 'Discover', and older guides describe discovering as driving or entering a vehicle.
dispute.call: Scanning is the reported method and the faster one — scan first, and only drive a model if its scan refuses to register.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Drop five enemies during one Combat Focus. Fill the Focus meter first, then pick a fight with enough targets clustered together — five in one slow-motion window is the whole ask.

steps.text: Fill the Combat Focus meter before you start — enter Focus with a full bar, not half of one.
Pick a fight with at least five enemies close together; gang members are the reported reliable target.
Trigger Combat Focus with an assault rifle and take down five enemies before the meter runs out.
Use the counter below to track the best run; the trophy pops when five fall in one activation.
If the count stalls, retry the same fight — the attempt costs nothing but the Focus meter.

dispute.versionA: GTABase reports that gang members count, and that cops, soldiers and civilians do not appear to count.
dispute.versionB: The trophy text says five enemies with no qualifier, which reads as any enemy.
dispute.call: Fight gang members — they satisfy both readings, while cops and civilians satisfy only the loose one.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Steal a departing passenger aircraft from Vice City International Airport and fly away with it. The description is a riddle; the method is a straight theft — get on the plane, get it moving, get out.

steps.text: Go to Vice City International Airport and find a docked passenger jet on the apron.
Board the jet and get it moving — the trophy is about the departure, not the destination.
Fly about a kilometre away from the airport to register the unscheduled departure.
The trophy pops once the jet is airborne and clear of the airport.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: Steal a Rhino military tank and use it in combat. The tank sits at a military site, so expect a fight to get in — and a bigger one once you are driving it.

steps.text: Go to Mile Zero Air Station, where the Rhino tanks are parked.
Steal a Rhino — expect armed resistance on the way in.
Use the tank's cannon in combat and take out enemies from inside it.
The trophy pops once the tank has seen combat under your control.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Clean out a jewelry store without anyone spotting you. The back door is the way in — quiet entry, quiet safe, quiet exit, and the trophy is yours.

steps.text: Pick a jewelry store and enter through its back door with the Snap Gun.
Find the safe code inside and open the safe without tripping an alarm.
Clear out the safe and leave the store without anyone spotting you.
If you are spotted, the attempt fails — leave, lose the heat, and try another store.
The trophy pops when the robbery completes undetected.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Rob five bank vaults and escape each time. The vaults open only after the optional Chapter 4 mission That's Where The Money Is… — miss that mission and the vaults stay locked, which is why this trophy sits on the watch list.

steps.text: Play the optional Chapter 4 mission That's Where The Money Is… — without it, the large bank vaults never open.
After the mission, follow a security van into a bank while its vault is open.
Rob the vault, then escape — expect four stars on the way out, so have a fast bike ready.
Repeat for five vaults; the checklist wants eight, so keep going if you are chasing A Long Road.
Use the counter below to track vaults robbed; the trophy pops at five.
Do the vaults before the story ends — the optional mission is the gate, and it belongs to Chapter 4.

dispute.versionA: The trophy needs 5 bank vaults robbed and escaped.
dispute.versionB: The 100% checklist needs 8 vaults hit, and both numbers appear in the same guides.
dispute.call: 5 for the trophy, 8 for the checklist — same vaults, different finish lines.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Hit an armored truck and get away with the cash. Trucks run set routes around the state — find one, stop it, crack it, and leave before the response arrives.

steps.text: Find an armored truck on its route — they run through Vice City and the highways.
Stop the truck and rob it; the rear doors are the way into the cash.
Escape with the cash and lose any wanted level that follows.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Reveal every part of the map. The fog lifts as you travel, and the fastest way to clear the last dark patches is from the air — fly over them and the map fills in underneath you.

steps.text: Travel every region of Leonida on foot, by road and by air — the fog clears where you have been.
Flying over the dark patches is reported as the quickest way to clear them.
Check the map for remaining fog after each region; the far corners and the Keys are the usual stragglers.
The trophy pops when the last patch of fog lifts and the whole state is revealed.
Pair the flying with WAiNK scans and stunt runs so the airtime does triple duty.

dispute.versionA: eGamers reports that flying over the dark patches is the quickest method to clear the fog.
dispute.versionB: Other guides describe exploring as driving every road, which reads as if flight alone is not enough.
dispute.call: Fly to clear the fog, then drive any patch that stays dark — the map itself is the judge, not the vehicle.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob one Illegal Operation from each of the nine gangs. Gang Operations are the backbone of the robbery checklist too — 39 in total — so this trophy is one stop on a much longer road.

steps.text: Open the Gang Operations list and note which of the nine gangs you have not hit yet.
Rob one Illegal Operation belonging to each gang — nine gangs, nine hits.
The checklist wants all 39 Gang Operations cleared, so keep clearing them after this pops.
Use the counter below to track gangs hit; the trophy pops at nine.
Vary the approach per gang — some operations are guarded, others are quiet smash-and-grabs.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Have a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach. The description is the whole instruction — the only open question is the exact trigger, which the guides have not fully pinned down.

steps.text: Go to Ocean Beach in Vice City and find a bar or vendor with a view of the water.
Order and enjoy a cocktail while facing the beach — the trophy is about the moment, not a mission.
If it does not pop at the first bar, try another beachfront spot; the exact trigger is still being confirmed.

dispute.versionA: GTAScoop reports it as enjoying a cocktail on Ocean Beach, with no further condition.
dispute.versionB: KeenGamer notes the exact trigger is still being confirmed, and eGamers lists the steps as unconfirmed.
dispute.call: The beach and the cocktail are agreed; the trigger is not. Try the beachfront bars in order and treat a non-pop as a wrong bar, not a wrong trophy.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Break out of a vehicle showroom through the glass, in classic GTA style. The description is a movie reference; the method is a car, a showroom window, and speed.

steps.text: Pick a vehicle showroom with a big glass front and drive a car inside or up to it.
One guide reports the method as crashing a car out through the showroom window.
Smash out through the glass at speed and the trophy should pop on the exit.

dispute.versionA: GTABase reports the method as crashing a car out through a showroom window.
dispute.versionB: PowerPyx marks the trophy as not yet known, with no confirmed method.
dispute.call: The window crash is the only published method and it matches the description word for word — try it first, and treat a non-pop as a wrong showroom.

trophies.name: Let's Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Steal the three key valuables at the Kolt & Associates bowling alley and get out. It is a small heist with a bowling theme — in quiet, out with the goods.

steps.text: Go to the Kolt & Associates bowling alley and case the three key valuables inside.
Steal the three valuables — the follow-through is the whole job.
Escape the alley with the valuables; the trophy pops on a clean getaway.
If the alarm goes up, leave and come back — a failed attempt costs nothing but the trip.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: Max out the Strength stat for both Jason and Lucia. Training is a slow grind, so fold it into the long cleanup stage — a few sessions between other jobs beats one long gym marathon.

steps.text: Find gyms and training spots around Leonida and work on the Strength stat.
Train with Jason until his Strength is maxed, then switch to Lucia and do the same.
Meditation also raises Focus, not Strength — do not mix the two grinds up.
The trophy pops when both characters sit at maximum Strength.
Spread the sessions across the cleanup stage; the stat rises a little at a time.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: Perform 500 actions that change your Criminal Profile. The profile tracks everything — robberies, driving, choices — so this trophy is a counter for playing the game like a criminal, and it fills itself across the whole run.

steps.text: Open the Criminal Profile screen to see which actions move it and where your count stands.
Play normally and the count climbs: robberies, stick-ups, getaways and story choices all feed it.
500 actions is the reported target — one guide's figure, so treat the profile screen as the authority.
Check the profile before the end of the cleanup stage; if you are short, run a batch of stick-ups.
Use the counter below to track your running total.

dispute.versionA: GTABase reports 500 actions that change the Criminal Profile as the target.
dispute.versionB: No second guide confirms the number, and PowerPyx does not list it — it is single-source.
dispute.call: Single-source, but the profile screen shows the live count, so the game itself settles it — trust the screen over either guide.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: Nobody has pinned this one down yet. The description — 'Second time's the charm' — suggests retrying something that failed once, but no guide has published a confirmed method. This entry says so plainly instead of inventing one.

steps.text: No guide has confirmed the unlock yet — PowerPyx and KeenGamer both list the method as unconfirmed.
The description hints at a second attempt succeeding where the first failed; watch for a retry-based trigger as the community reports back.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: Nobody has pinned this one down yet. The description suggests a strange event somewhere in Leonida, but no guide has confirmed where or what. This entry says so plainly instead of inventing a location.

steps.text: No guide has confirmed the unlock yet — PowerPyx and KeenGamer both list the method as unconfirmed.
One guide reports it refers to a strange event somewhere in Leonida, though that is not confirmed either.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock someone over with a melee drive-by — a melee swing from a moving vehicle. The description names the move; the open question is the precise setup, so the steps below give the version the guides agree on and flag the rest.

steps.text: Get in a vehicle with a melee weapon equipped and find a target on foot.
Drive past and swing the melee weapon from the vehicle — the drive-by is the trigger, not the kill.
If it does not pop, vary the vehicle and the weapon; the precise method is still being confirmed.

dispute.versionA: KeenGamer confirms the action is a melee drive-by but says the precise method is still being confirmed.
dispute.versionB: The trophy text itself names the move — 'Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by' — with no further condition.
dispute.call: The move is confirmed, the setup is not — try a car first, then a bike, and treat a non-pop as a wrong setup.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Launder $250,000 in Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked Bills pile up from robberies all game long, and the same $250,000 is a line on the 100% checklist — so this trophy is a receipt for robbing well.

steps.text: Marked Bills come from robberies — bank jobs, vaults and stick-ups all pay in them.
Launder them through your contacts and fences; one fence pays the most, so use the best rate you have unlocked.
The total grows during the 100% robberies, so do not grind it separately until the checklist is nearly done.
Use the counter below to track dollars laundered; the trophy pops at $250,000.
The same $250,000 is a 100% checklist line, so this trophy and A Long Road share the work.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops. Weapons, clothes, cars, food — every dollar counts, and by the time you have bought the garages and the gear for the rest of the run, this trophy is usually already yours.

steps.text: Spend money in any shop — weapons, clothing, vehicles and food all count toward the total.
Big purchases (weapons and cars) move the counter fastest; do not grind it with snacks.
Use the counter below to track dollars spent; the trophy pops at $100,000.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Buy all eight purchasable garages in the Vice City Real Estate app. The four garages the story gives you do not count — only the eight you buy with your own money.

steps.text: Open the Vice City Real Estate app on the in-game phone and list the purchasable garages.
Buy all eight garages — around $160,000 in total, so bring the cash from your robbery runs.
The four story garages do not count toward the eight.
Use the counter below to track garages owned; the trophy pops at eight.

dispute.versionA: KeenGamer says eight purchasable garage properties.
dispute.versionB: eGamers agrees on eight, and adds that the four story garages do not count — which some readers mix up into twelve.
dispute.call: Eight bought, four story garages excluded — the app shows the eight, so buy what the app lists.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register ten vehicles through the Scooter Bros app. Any ten cars will do — street cars are the fastest filler, so grab, register, repeat.

steps.text: Open the Scooter Bros app on the in-game phone and check the registration screen.
Register ten different vehicles; cheap street cars are the fastest way to fill the slots.
Use the counter below to track registrations; the trophy pops at ten.
